clue.text: Pays for conservative’s false alibi

blocks.note: to cover a bill is to pay it
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party; the 's is just the surface

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician pays to have a false alibi drawn up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after conservative joins the two pieces in the surface and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cover story is an invented account meant to hide what really happened, much like a made-up excuse for one's whereabouts.

clue.text: Faith in mediocre education

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words that follow, running across them

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone's religious faith rests on a second-rate schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: Mediocre seems to want a grade abbreviation, but the letters are simply read straight through the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a set of religious beliefs, so it can stand for a person's religion or belief system.

clue.text: Broken coal ovens — they can produce lots of smoke!

definitions.text: they can produce lots of smoke!

indicators.note: something broken has its parts scattered, so the letters of the next words are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Faulty coal-fired ovens are belching out clouds of smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful description rather than a dictionary synonym, which the exclamation mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Erupting mountains throw up huge plumes of ash and gas, so they are things capable of pouring out enormous clouds.

clue.text: Weapon search

blocks.note: first meaning: a long-barrelled gun
second meaning: to rummage through something hurriedly

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a hunt for a gun; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a shoulder-fired firearm and a verb for ransacking drawers or pockets.

clue.text: Leaders in The Oval Office, also

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so we take the opening letter of each following word

blocks.note: the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: The heads of government in the White House's Oval Office are mentioned too.
explanation.definitionFit: Too and also are interchangeable adverbs meaning in addition or as well.

clue.text: I reused horrible leftovers

definitions.note: plural in the clue; the answer is a mass noun covering the same remains

indicators.note: horrible suggests something messed up and ugly, so the preceding words are jumbled

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to serving up nasty leftovers again.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is whatever remains after the main part has gone, which is what leftovers are.

clue.text: Bachelor on island failing to finish liquor?

indicators.note: failing to finish means stopping short, so the last letter of the island is dropped

blocks.note: a bachelor is an unmarried man
the Mediterranean island nation

explanation.surface: An unmarried man on holiday on an island can't finish his drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks liquor as a definition by example: single malt is one kind of liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Single malt is a whisky distilled from malted barley at one distillery, a type of spirit.

clue.text: What a casino employee might say is perfect?

blocks.clueFragment: What a casino employee might say
blocks.note: a croupier hands out the cards and could announce that he or she is dealing, in two short words

explanation.surface: A riddle about the right line for a croupier at the card table.
explanation.walkthrough: The first-person pronoun I plus DEAL, as a dealer might announce, runs together into a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal describes something that is flawless and exactly as it should be, the best possible.

clue.text: Ship’s wreckage — beginning to find plenty in the morning

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of find
lots means a great deal, plenty
a.m. marks times before noon

explanation.surface: A beachcomber finds a mass of shipwreck debris washed up one morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Flotsam is the floating debris left after a vessel sinks or breaks up, as distinct from jetsam thrown overboard.

clue.text: Psychic put fear into underground worker

indicators.note: put with into tells us one word is placed inside another

blocks.note: a miner works below ground
dread is great fear

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant frightened a coal miner.
explanation.walkthrough: Psychic sits first in the clue and is the definition; the rest is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychic claims to know other people's thoughts, which is exactly what a mind reader does.

clue.text: Pet dragon is strange baptism participant!

indicators.note: being strange means being odd or out of order, so the preceding letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Someone's pet dragon turning up at a christening would be odd.
explanation.definitionFit: At a christening, sponsors stand alongside the child and promise to oversee its religious upbringing.

clue.text: I chuck in worn-out fossil

indicators.note: in tells us the first pieces go inside the word that follows

blocks.note: trite means stale and overused
taken as written
to lob is to throw or chuck

explanation.surface: Someone throws an old, worn-out fossil away.
explanation.walkthrough: Fossil looks like it could describe something worn-out, but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Trilobites are extinct marine arthropods whose remains are among the commonest fossils found in ancient rocks.

clue.text: Eat briefly, making racket

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter is lopped off

blocks.note: to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: Someone eats a quick meal while making a lot of noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A din is a loud, confused noise, the same as a racket in its sense of uproar.

clue.text: Drink, for example, with medal being returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
gong is British slang for a medal or honour

explanation.surface: A drink is offered, say, while a medal gets handed back.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a gong is a medal or award.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggnog is a festive beverage made of eggs, milk, sugar and often spirits.

clue.text: Fool picked up then let go of sweet

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking something up lifts it, so the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a mug is a gullible person, a fool
to drop something is to let go of it; then just orders the pieces

explanation.surface: A clumsy person picked up a sweet and then dropped it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like a homophone signal, but in a down entry it lifts MUG upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A gumdrop is a small chewy confection, a type of candy.

clue.text: Inability to catch, or retain, strangely

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the preceding letters come out in an odd order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A fielder who can't hold a catch, or hang onto anything at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Catch here means hearing or picking up a tune, not catching a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a tin ear cannot pick up musical pitch or subtle tones, an inability to hear things properly.

clue.text: Supply department

blocks.note: first meaning: to equip with weapons
second meaning: a branch or division of an organisation

explanation.walkthrough: Together they suggest a supply department; separately each is a meaning of the short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for furnishing troops with guns and a noun for one branch of a larger body, like a company's sales wing.

clue.text: Therefore a religious leader initially records a drama

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: so means therefore
taken as written
the head of the Roman Catholic Church
the opening letter of records
the second a, taken as written

explanation.surface: So a church leader is first to record a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Both a's in the clue are used as letters; drama alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running serial on television or radio, a kind of melodramatic show.

clue.text: Contents of data, stick found in storage area

indicators.note: contents are what lies inside, so the outer letters are discarded and the inner ones kept

blocks.note: the inner letters of data
the inner letters of stick

explanation.surface: A data stick turns up in the storeroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a USB memory stick; the contents indicator applies to both words, each losing its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the space under a roof, typically used for keeping boxes and unused belongings.

clue.text: Tests new axes around military, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter is taken
new suggests a fresh arrangement, so those letters are reordered
around tells us the rearranged letters surround the selected one

blocks.note: the opening letter of military
the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Soldiers try out new axes.
explanation.definitionFit: Exams are formal assessments of knowledge, the same thing as tests at school or college.

clue.text: Flood from river covering moor regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
covering means wrapping round, so the river goes around the kept letters

blocks.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands
the second and fourth letters of moor

explanation.surface: A flood pours off a moor when a river overflows.
explanation.walkthrough: River usually gives R, but here a named river is needed: the Trent flows through the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a violent rushing stream of water, so it can stand for a flood.

clue.text: Study agreement in speech

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken, so we want a word sounding like the one indicated

blocks.note: aye is a word of assent, yes

explanation.surface: Studying how people express agreement in their talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look at it closely, so it works as a verb meaning to examine.

clue.text: Blackbeard, say, doesn’t start being angry

indicators.note: not starting means the opening letter is missing

blocks.note: Blackbeard was a notorious eighteenth-century pirate; say marks him as an example

explanation.surface: The pirate Blackbeard won't get going and is furious about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate is a synonym meaning furious or incensed.

clue.text: A quick game with mates?

blocks.note: surface reading: a fast round of something played with friends
setter's reading: mates are checkmates, and the game is a chess variant played against the clock

explanation.walkthrough: Mates looks like friends, but in chess a mate ends the game.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a form of chess where each player has only a few minutes on the clock for all moves.
